thread:
elaine: Hey team — customer reporting intermittent 401s during streaming behind a corporate proxy. They see request IDs 01G7XY2A3B and 01G7XY2A3C in our logs. Behavior: initial chunks stream fine, then connection closes with no error body. They can repro with curl but it sometimes finishes cleanly, sometimes ends mid-stream.

elaine: Customer gave this minimal repro they ran from a Windows box with a proxy: 
```
curl -v --no-buffer \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED_TOKEN" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  --proxy http://corp-proxy.local:8080 \
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams/generate?model=redwood-1
```

elaine: They attached a short verbose dump showing TLS ALPN negotiated to h2 then proxy logs show a CONNECT then 200, but client later shows "EOF" and our backend logs show the same request id but no final status.

mateo: Thanks — a few asks to triage quickly:
1) Can they re-run with trace and an explicit X-Request-ID so we can correlate client tcpdump and our server logs? Example command: 
```
curl -v --no-buffer --trace-ascii /tmp/curl.trace \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED_TOKEN" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -H "X-Request-ID: local-elaine-01G7XY2A3B" \
  --proxy http://corp-proxy.local:8080 \
  --http2 \
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams/generate?model=redwood-1
```
Also ask them to attach /tmp/curl.trace.

mateo: If possible, capture a short packet trace while reproducing (tcpdump -w /tmp/stream.pcap port 443) so we can see whether the proxy abruptly resets or whether the server stops sending.

devon: On our side I checked the traces for 01G7XY2A3B and 01G7XY2A3C — both show streaming started, tokens emitted, then no final completion event within the expected timeout window (30s). There was a brief auth-rotation event around that timeframe but not a token rejection. Can we confirm if the proxy is altering chunked framing?

harper: Two quick checks for the customer to run to narrow proxy vs TLS layer:
- Verify ALPN negotiated: 
```
openssl s_client -connect api.redwood.example:443 -alpn h2 -servername api.redwood.example
```
Look for "ALPN protocol: h2". If proxy terminates TLS for inspection, ALPN may be different or absent.

- Try bypassing proxy for a quick smoke if policy allows: set HTTP_PROXY empty or use a machine not behind corp-proxy. If bypass works consistently, root cause is likely proxy mutating stream frames.

harper: Also ask them to try forcing http/1.1 to see if behavior changes: 
```
curl -v --no-buffer --http1.1 -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED_TOKEN" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  --proxy http://corp-proxy.local:8080 \
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams/generate?model=redwood-1
```
If h2 fails but h1.1 works (or vice versa) that's useful.

deploy-bot: Note: auth-rotation service-deploy v2024.9.11 rolled at 2024-09-11T15:08:42Z (no errors reported).

devon: I'll pull the backend side logs for these IDs and look for any upstream resets or client disconnect frames. If we see FIN from client at X second mark, that'll indicate client/proxy closed. If we see no FIN but no more write attempts, might be server-side issue.

elaine: I'll ask customer to collect: curl.trace, tcpdump pcap, and the exact proxy logs for the CONNECT session. I'll send them a short checklist and the two modified curl commands (with X-Request-ID and --trace-ascii).

elaine: Quick checklist I'll send to customer: 
• Re-run with trace: add --trace-ascii /tmp/curl.trace and -H "X-Request-ID: <their-local-id>"
• Capture pcap: tcpdump -w /tmp/stream.pcap port 443 (or port their proxy uses) during repro
• Try bypassing proxy if allowed OR try forcing --http1.1 to compare
• Attach curl.trace, stream.pcap, and proxy CONNECT logs, and note which X-Request-ID maps to which file

mateo: Once they attach, please upload to the support bundle and ping me. I can run a quick passive parse for chunk boundaries and any unexpected RST/FINs.

elaine: Will do. Thanks team :thumbsup:
